title: Ground-field retagging identifies ordinary strict-tower operations
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$, an algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with ring of integers $\mathcal O_E$; put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-pur-conventions, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and $f:X\to Y$ a smooth separated $k$-morphism of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For a field automorphism $\sigma:k\simeq k$ fixing $k_0$, let $T^\sigma$ be the same scheme $T$ with structural map $\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)\circ a_T$, for $T=X,Y$, and let $f^\sigma$ be the same underlying morphism. Use the strict varying-coefficient tower categories $\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E)$ [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers], their ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and their full subcategories $\mathcal C_T=\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$ of towers with constructible levels and level-independent finite cohomological and Tor bounds [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers].

The identity on the underlying small pro-etale ringed sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] identifies the abelian categories $\operatorname{Tow}(T^\sigma,\mathcal O_E)=\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E)$, including the coefficient quotient maps and semilinear transitions, and identifies their categories of complexes, quasi-isomorphisms, ordinary derived categories and subcategories $\mathcal C_T$. Under these identifications, the exact tower pullbacks for $f^\sigma$ and $f$ agree; the ordinary derived tower tensor products over $(A_{n,T})_n$ agree, with their unit, symmetry, associativity and pullback-tensor comparisons; and the levelwise Tate twists agree, with their power and quotient transitions and their twist reassociations [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels, def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. For a chosen compactification $X\xrightarrow j\overline X\xrightarrow pY$ of $f$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], give $\overline X$ the retagged structural map as well. The ordinary tower compact-support functors $F=Rp_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}$ for the two presentations are identified on bounded-below towers, together with the underlying pullback/direct-image adjunctions and extension-by-zero tensor comparisons [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. All these are identifications of tower constructions before finite evaluation; they retain the actual quotient-coefficient transitions. No derived reduction-isomorphism condition on the input towers is imposed.

proof.text: The functor Over.map postcomposes the structure map only. Its object left and morphism left projections reduce to the original scheme and arrow. The retagged compactification is defined to be the original compactification. Thus the sites, coefficient diagrams, tower and complex categories, quasi-isomorphisms, calculus, derived categories, constructible/Tor predicates and inclusions, roots, integral lines, finite quotients, signed lines, geometry, pullback, compact support and open operations are identified by reflexivity. No new adjunction, resolution or tensor comparison is selected.

For two normalized quotient-comparison families, degree-one homomorphisms agree on double scalar-extension pure sections by their common multiplication formula. scalarExtensionTower_hom_ext gives equality of degree-one isomorphisms. At zero use the normalized unit formula. Induct on nonnegative powers, using scalarExtension_tensor_hom_ext and the positive recursion to compare both factor images. For each negative power use its prescribed dual-map composite and the equality of the positive isomorphism, including its inverse. Function extensionality gives equality of families; substitution then identifies every semilinear transition.

The DVR computation in spEllIdeal_eq_uniformizer_pow gives a positive e with (ell)=(varpi)^e. Hence the ideal at level n is the uniformizer ideal at positive exponent e(n+1). Regard ordinary scalar extension of the integral Tate line as a family indexed by its quotient ideal and transport along this equality. The finite local-freeness clause of pur_twist_sheaf_locally_free makes this line locally free of rank one. Its hypothesis holds because the prime ell is a unit in the stalks of every k-scheme by the purity setting and remains a unit in the residue fields. Rank-one local freeness supplies a CoversTop family of isomorphisms with free modules of rank one, then freeUniqueIso identifies these with the scalar units. existsUnique_signedLineProduct applied to this cover identifies any two normalized product families. Empty schemes cause no exception: covers and uniqueness are valid there as well. Assemble all conjunctions without changing any hypothesis.

tool_uses.why: Common tower category is abelian and evaluation is exact; generic input rather than an alternative purity route.
Ordinary derived tensor and geometric adjunctions on arbitrary strict ring systems; no normalization or flat-transition assumption.
Supplies the adjunction-normalized tensor comparison for arbitrary inverse ring sequences, including powers of ell.
Computes bounded-below tower direct image by an injective tower resolution.
Finite Tate twists are rank-one lines so signed dual and quotient comparisons apply.
Signed powers, dual quotient maps and twist reassociations are canonically normalized on local bases.
Characterizes open tensor comparison by its adjoint inverse, explicitly for arbitrary strict systems.
